title: Launch orchestra staffing heuristics and clockwork checklist — Apr 2028 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working sketch for the next multi-region launch (window: Apr 20–27, 2028). It combines staffing heuristics, a lightweight clockwork-style checklist for day-of operators, an escalation / decision ladder, and an annotated release-notes draft intended for downstream product & CS edits.

Goals & constraints (high level):
- Keep latency SLOs during gradual traffic ramp and fallbacks.
- Avoid broad rollbacks where feasible; prefer micro-rollbacks + traffic-shifts.
- Minimize engineer interruption by codifying common decision points and default actions.
- Provide a short release note seed so customer-facing teams can iterate.

Launch window snapshot:
- Canary start: 2028-04-20 09:00 PT (region: us-west1 only)
- Micro-rollout cohort expansion: 2028-04-20 12:00 → 20:00 PT (incremental 5→25→50→100% within cohort)
- Multi-region ramp (if green): 2028-04-21 02:00 PT (eu-west1 warmup), 2028-04-21 14:00 PT (asia-east1 warmup)
- Full global traffic target: 2028-04-27 00:00 PT

Staffing heuristics (how many people, where):
- Day-of on-call (primary ops): 1 SRE (lead), 1 Release Engineer, 1 Observability SME. 24h coverage via baton handoff if rollout spans >12h.
- Canary shepherds (for incremental cohorts): 2 engineers (serving-runtime + model-routing). They own KV-cache priming, model variant toggles.
- Customer escalation lane: 1 CSE on standby for top Enterprise customers; escalate through PM/EM if incidents reach P1s.
- Night/second-shift (if multi-day): 1 SRE (night), 1 Release Engineer (on-call), product owner on brief rotation.
- Backup capacity lead: 1 infra engineer who can trigger instance pools / capacity-bumps for Dedicated tenants.

Sizing guidance (quick rules):
- If expected QPS < 2k and canary is single region: lean staffing (combine SRE & Release Engineer roles).
- If expected QPS 2k–10k: full roster above.
- If expected QPS > 10k or heavy embeddings workload: add an additional infra/ops lead and a model-QC engineer.

Clockwork checklist (operator-friendly, day-of):
Pre-launch (T-72 → T-2 hours):
  - T-72: Finalize release notes draft; confirm all linked artifacts exist. (Owner: Release PM)
  - T-48: Run preflight traffic replay against staging kernel; check 95/99th latency diff < +15% vs baseline. (Owner: Observability)
  - T-24: Confirm feature flags and model pins are set in config. Check rollout policy in console. (Owner: Release Eng)
  - T-6: Hotlist 10 customers that should not be included in canary; ensure ACLs. (Owner: CSE)
  - T-1: Smoke test the canary route with synthetic long-sequence prompts, KV-cache priming script. (Owner: Serving Runtime)
  - T-0.5: Confirm pager rotations and Slack bridge are up. Post brief in #release-ops. (Owner: Release Lead)

Canary / Micro-rollout (T+0 → T+12 hours):
  - Start with 1% traffic to canary. Monitor: latency (p50/p95/p99), error rate, tokens/sec, model sync failures. (Owner: Canary Shepherd)
  - At each increment (1→5→25→50), run 20–30 minute observation windows. For each window, if any of the below thresholds are exceeded, STOP and initiate decision ladder.

Decision thresholds (auto-stop criteria):
  - p99 latency > baseline_p99 * 1.8 for 2 consecutive windows
  - Error rate > 0.5% (user-facing errors) or > 1% (internal retriable errors)
  - Token generation anomalies: sudden token length truncation or repeated tokens >3x baseline
  - Model mismatch: output distribution divergence (semantic regression) flagged by eval-runner (see linked Artifacts)

Decision ladder (ordered actions on stop):
  - Step 1: Revert traffic to previous cohort percentage (e.g., 25% -> 5%). Document timestamp & reason.
  - Step 2: If issue persists, switch to fallback model variant that is binary-compatible (pre-approved): run 30m watch.
  - Step 3: If still failing, pause rollout and open postmortem-runbook channel; if customer impact > P1, trigger incident and engage oncall SE.
  - Step 4: For capacity/infra failures only: activate backup capacity pool and scale autoscaling thresholds up by +20% for 60 minutes.

Observability & telemetry quick-checks (what to scan):
- Traffic routing logs: confirm no silent misroutes (route mismatch > 0.1% indicates config bug).
- Token-level cost spike: investigate caching misses or sudden SLO increases.
- Model-serving error codes: KV cache misses vs kernel OOMs categorized.
- Quality sampling: run daily 200-sample eval set for canary cohort, check Rouge/BLEU-style markers + simple semantic sanity checks.

Rollback vs Hold vs Quick-fix guidance:
- Rollback when: repeated p99 spikes coincident with error-rate or model regressions and fallback fails.
- Hold and debug when: intermittent spikes tied to infra ops (disk/network) and workarounds exist (scale-up, drain nodes).
- Quick-fix allowed when: small config mistake (flag, route) and can be reversed in <10 minutes without client impact.

Annotated release notes (seed for product/CS) — DRAFT
Title: Incremental inference optimizations + model-routing resiliency
What’s changing:
- Serving runtime: improved KV cache priming to reduce cold-start token costs for long conversations.
- Routing: new fallback model variant for medium-latency inference workloads; auto-fallback policy configurable per project.
- Console: per-route rollout progress now shows cohort sizes and last-observed p99 latency.
Who it affects:
- Most apps: no action required.
- Customers with very strict latency budgets: see migration notes below (pin older model or enable conservative throttles).
Known limitations / notes:
- Initial canary will be limited to us-west1 — global rollouts will follow in the week after validation.
- Dedicated clusters: if you use strict isolation, reach out to CSE to schedule a staggered rollout.

Action items (short) — owner tags in parentheses:
- Finalize fallback model variant list and link to model-catalog (Rafael)
- Add traffic-priming script to infra repo and test in canary-staging (Jonah)
- Update per-route dashboard templates and add alerting guard rails (Observability team)
- Draft customer-facing release note and prepare FAQ (Product & CS)

Unresolved questions / open decisions:
- Should we include embeddings-heavy customers in the first multi-region wave? (pros: increased exercise; cons: risk to token cost spikes) — decision pending with PM by Apr 15.
- Autoscaling safety margin during initial ramp: +20% is a default; confirm if we should temporarily increase to +35% for Dedicated to avoid saturation.

Mini retrospective template (post-launch):
- 24h: quick check-in — did any cohort require pause? Reason & mitigation used.
- 72h: collect sample diffs and customer tickets; tag any quality regressions.
- 7d: write short launch debrief (what worked, what surprised us, followups).

Notes to self / quick hints:
- Use the release-runner script (infra/scripts/release-runner.sh) to apply cohort deltas; it logs a compact audit trail.
- Keep the bridge pinned to the #release-ops Slack pinned items: canary-playbook, rollback-template, contact-roster.
- If model-quality drift is subtle, run the eval harness with a 500-sample prompt set — semantic regressions typically show up within 6–12 hours when traffic is representative.

Appendix — quick links and commands (for operators):
- Rollout change CLI: infractl rollout apply --route <route> --percent <n> --note "<reason>"
- Fallback toggle: console -> Route -> Advanced -> Fallback Model -> select variant
- Emergency rollback: infractl rollout revert --to-tag <previous-tag>

End of draft.

---
Explicit TODOs for this doc before finalizing:
1) Add a small table mapping expected QPS bands to recommended staffing (SRE/Release/Obs counts).
2) Get sign-off from Observability on the exact metric thresholds (p99 multiplier, error bins).
3) Attach the canonical eval set id and a reproducible script for automatic daily sampling.

If you are reading this and will be on the launch: add any missing quick-commands you rely on below or ping me (Maya) in #release-ops — I'll fold them into the next iteration.
